subject: Embeddings model-fit & validation — next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Lowe <ben.lowe@acmeretail.com>, Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: embeddings evaluation & next steps

Thanks for the time this morning — good conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Recap
- Use case: semantic product search across ACME's catalog (text + some short specs). Primary aim is better relevance for long-tail queries and brand synonyms.
- Current baseline: BM25 + heuristic boosting; internal evaluation reported recall@10 ~0.62 on the small validation set.
- Data: ~1.2M SKUs, working with a 1k golden query set (Sarah to confirm final set).
- Constraints: latency SLO ~50ms p95 for search per request, want vector index size to be reasonable (cost tradeoffs), and drift detection for seasonal catalog changes.

Proposed evaluation plan (ask)
1) We run a model-fit validation comparing two embedding models on your 1k golden queries + sampled negative set:
   - redwood-emb-small-v1 (256d)
   - open-embed-2 (1536d)
2) Metrics we'll report: recall@k (k=1,5,10), MRR, average cosine distance distributions, and index size (RAM per 1M vectors).
3) Action items for you: please upload the 1k query file and a small product sample (~10k rows) to the Drive folder linked below, or reply with a shared S3 link.

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.jsonl (basic query transformations); I can iterate on prompt variants if you want to surface synonyms/brand normalization.

Next steps
- If you confirm upload, I’ll run the first-pass bench (expected turnaround 24–48h) and share a short report + recommended model/config.
- Propose a 30-min sync after I share results to decide indexing (PQ/IVF/Faiss config) and production rollout plan.

Thanks — looking forward to the sample data.

—
Marcus Lin

Thanks Marcus — great summary. Sarah and I chatted after the demo and we can confirm the 1k golden queries; I'll upload them and a 10k product sample to the Drive folder by EOD. A few clarifications:

- The team prefers the smaller index footprint (cost is a hard constraint), but we care most about recall@5 for help center style queries.
- Latency target is client-facing search; approx 50ms p95 is ideal.
- We do have an internal user feedback signal (click-through conversion) that we'd like to incorporate into eval as a secondary metric.

I'll upload files and ping here once they're available. Thanks for moving quickly on the bench.

Best,

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Ben — saw the upload, thanks. I kicked off the bench on the 1k golden queries + 10k sample subset. Preliminary plan and recommendations below so you know what to expect in the report:

Bench plan
- Models: redwood-emb-small-v1 (256d, float16) and open-embed-2 (1536d, float32)
- Index configs: HNSW (PQ 64/IVF fallback) for the 1536d run; Flat/HNSW hybrid for 256d to hit latency SLO.
- Metrics: recall@1/5/10, MRR, mean cosine distance, per-query variance, and index memory footprint (GB/1M vectors).
- Drift check: we'll compute embedding drift vs last-month snapshot (cosine shift distribution) and per-category cluster centroid shift.

Initial recommendations (subject to final results)
- If recall@5 delta between 256d and 1536d is < 6 points and index size difference causes >2x cost, prefer redwood-emb-small-v1 with periodic fine-tuning and synonym preprocessing.
- If 1536d shows >8 points lift on recall@5 for long-tail queries, recommend a hybrid: use 256d for most traffic and route ambiguous/long-form queries to the higher-dim model (model routing can keep p95 latency within SLO).

Attached: embeddings_benchmarks_20270328.csv (interim results), prompt_set_v2.jsonl (updated prompt variants). Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folder/1a2b3c-acme-embeddings-benchmarks

Can we book a 30-min review tomorrow at 10am PT? If that doesn't work, propose 2pm PT.

Thanks — will include Rishi for any quantization/throughput tradeoff questions.

—
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: embeddings evaluation & next steps — bench plan + initial recommendations

Nice work getting the bench started. A couple of operational items to call out from the product/QA side:

- Quality-regression monitoring: we should establish a baseline evaluation and set regression thresholds (e.g., MRR drop > 3% or recall@5 drop > 4% triggers an alert). Add a canary rollout policy if they move to the higher-dim model.
- Prompt/normalization drift: capture a sample of weekly queries and re-run the eval set monthly to detect distributional shifts (seasonal catalog changes).
- Dimensionality/quantization note for Rishi: if we recommend the 1536d model, consider 8-bit quantization experiments and measure MMR impact; log per-token latency and memory footprint at the client-side to ensure the 50ms p95 target.

Marcus — I can take lead on the regression dashboard templates and the alert thresholds if you want; Rishi, can you scope the quantization experiments (run on a 10k-vector subset) and confirm expected throughput numbers?

Thanks — I’ll join the review tomorrow.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
